name: Bvlgari Hotel, Milano
positioning: Five-star hotel (officially The Bvlgari Hotel Milano) in a renovated 18th-century palazzo near Via Montenapoleone, La Scala and Brera, with a large private garden
best_for: Travelers who want a central Milan base near La Scala and Brera
Guests who want a private garden and concierge-arranged excursions

facts.text: The hotel is on a private street in downtown Milan, between Via Montenapoleone, Via della Spiga, La Scala and the Accademia di Brera.
The hotel has a 4,000-square-meter private garden, described as a natural extension of the nearby Botanical Garden.
The earliest mention of the original layout of the hotel garden is in the Ruralium Commodorum by Piero de Crescenza, from 1305.
Guests can visit the adjacent Botanical Garden inside the Palazzo di Brera, which also hosts the Pinacoteca.
The hotel organizes private visits to villas and museums, hydroplane trips around Lake Como and excursions to Italian destinations by private plane, limousine or yacht.
Services include a personal shopper, personal trainer, luxury car rental, in-room check-in, assistance with packing and unpacking, and a parking garage.
Premium Rooms face either the garden or a Milanese courtyard.
Premium Suites are on private floors with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the adjoining Botanical Gardens.

highlights.text: The hotel has a 4,000-square-meter private garden, described as a natural extension of the nearby Botanical Garden.
The lounge fireplace is made of black Zimbabwe granite and weighs 15 tonnes.
The earliest mention of the original layout of the hotel garden is in the Ruralium Commodorum by Piero de Crescenza, from 1305.
The Bvlgari Suite is a 160 sqm one-bedroom suite with a design curated by architect Flaviano Capriotti.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive positioning.
WhataHotel notes limited room inventory because of the boutique size of the hotel.
